text: A summary formula calculates on grouped totals. A row-level formula calculates on every individual record, before any grouping happens. Think of it as a computed column in your SELECT list.

Add one from the same Columns dropdown in the Outline panel. Three classic uses. First, classify each record: if Amount is over a hundred thousand, Large, otherwise check for Medium, else Small. Second, compute an age: today minus the created date, in days. Third, weight a value: Amount times Probability. Field tokens for standard fields often look like AMOUNT or CLOSE_DATE, so insert them from the editor.

The concept that matters most is the order of operations. Row-level formulas are evaluated first, for each record. Then the report filters, groups, and summarizes. Summary formulas run last, on the totals. That's why weighting and then summing needs a row-level formula, because multiplying two already-summed columns gives a different answer.

In SQL terms, the row-level formula is Amount times Probability as Weighted, or a CASE expression, inside the select list. The summary formula is the ratio of aggregates after GROUP BY. Once your weighted column exists, summarize it like any numeric field, and group by owner to get weighted pipeline.

If several reports keep re-creating the same expression, ask an admin for a permanent formula field on the object instead. Also note that a report can only hold a small number of row-level formulas, so check the current limit before you plan around several. Next up: the functions available for analysts.
